## Audit Summary

**Card**: Naturalize (`{1}{G}` Instant — Destroy target artifact or enchantment.)
**Status**: ISSUE

### Issue Found

**`is_valid_target` misses artifact/enchantment tokens** (`mtg-engine/src/cards/isd/naturalize.rs`, lines 40–42)

The function checks only `registry.card_data(obj.card_id)` to determine whether a battlefield permanent is an artifact or enchantment. Tokens are created with `card_id: CardId(0)` (a sentinel value registered to nothing), so `registry.card_data(CardId(0))` always returns `None`, and `.unwrap_or(false)` rejects the token as a valid target.

Tokens store their card types directly in `obj.card_types`, which this code never reads. The correct pattern — already used in `engine.rs`'s Stony Silence check (lines 280–283) — checks both sources:
```rust
registry.card_data(obj.card_id)
    .map(|d| d.card_types.contains(&CardType::Artifact))
    .unwrap_or(false)
    || obj.card_types.contains(&CardType::Artifact)
```

No artifact or enchantment tokens currently exist in the card set, so this bug does not affect any implemented scenario — but the implementation is structurally wrong and would silently prevent targeting (e.g.) a Gold, Treasure, or Clue token.

All other aspects — mana cost, type, oracle text field, `resolve_destroy` usage, `move_spell_after_resolve`, indestructible/regeneration handling — are correct.
